title: Cleo Brown's records and the demand for women pianist-singers
summary: Cleo Brown's boogie records and Hollywood booking made women pianist-singers in demand, which she says helped her.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: Well, if you think of it you could still let me know and we'll put it down in writing. You also mentioned that when you got here Cleo Brown was very popular in Los Angeles, and you mentioned she was from Chicago. But did she record? Was she well known for in person appearances or was she also a record artist?

Yes, she was very well known. She really made her -- got her recognition on records. In fact she was responsible for the change, you know, and for the demand for women piano players and singers. Because before that time -- and she was doing a boogie woogie thing, you know, and before that time I don't think too much attention was paid to women, you know, to women piano players and singers. Maybe that's why you didn't see too many of them with the bands, other than maybe a singer, a girl just singing. Cleo, when I first came to California, well her records were just all over. Even before I came to California, Cleo Brown was -- you know, she was well on her way. And I think when I came here, shortly after I got here, she was booked out here into one of the spots. I can't remember now even what the spot was, but she was booked in Hollywood, into one of the big spots here, and she was just

absolutely the -- just the talk of the town and the talk of the country, for that matter. And then after that time, really, then attention was focused on women. I really feel in a way that this was what sort of helped me, because at that time they were ready for -- you know, they were ready for women piano players and singers, because she sang and played, and she had her own little style, which was a tremendous style, and she had a terrific left hand, terrific boogie thing.
